title: Honest Regression-Discontinuity Bounds at Selected Escalation Cutoffs in Model Cascades
banked_reason: D0.5 repeatedly failed on selected-cutoff geometry, generated-score drift, and post-selection honest-CI gaps; the last review still required new math or definition repair beyond an in-place D0.R edit.
gap_reasons: Final D0.5 review made no net progress: width_term_omitted@lem:postselect-honest-ci-under-gates, CRUX_ASSUMED@conj:postselect-honest-ci, and frontier_contact_not_discharged@conj:active-set-geometry remained open.
The selected-cutoff active-set geometry depended on unsupported perfect-spline/finite affine-branch reductions: bad_parametric_reduction and NONAFFINE_REDUCTION_GAP at lem:perfect-spline-active-set.

The generated-score correction was self-discharging: def:generated-score-drift-handle treated hat G_n as a whole-gap envelope rather than primitive additive components with separate control, and lem:ghat-envelope-valid dropped a gap term.

The post-selection honest-CI rung lacked the empirical-process, selected-threshold localization, oracle-neighborhood coverage, and generated-score expansion ingredients needed to transfer fixed-cutoff honest RD to the selected feasible cutoff.
proof_attempt_summary: The run tried to build a field-tier selected-cutoff honest RD partial-ID result for LLM cascade escalation: a curvature-budget sharp interval for the boundary net value, a critical-curvature sign frontier, finite active-set geometry, and post-selection honest feasible inference with generated-score correction. Stage -0.5 accepted the topic, but D0.5 repeatedly found that the core assumed the hard parts: finite perfect-spline active-set structure, primitive generated-score drift control, and selected-threshold honest-CI process bounds. A retry should keep the selected-cutoff problem framing and literature map, but must either prove those gates directly or narrow the claim before rerunning discovery.
tldr: The proposal treats the selected LLM-cascade cutoff as a population-selected boundary problem whose primary object is the M-indexed interval [L_*(P,M), U_*(P,M)] generated by the local extension class H_*(P,M), not a uniquely observed-law point target in the atomic isotonic-score regime. The main theorem is an attainment result inside that pre-imposed class: once tau_*(P) and H_*(P,M) are fixed, the full set {mu(tau_*(P)) : mu in H_*(P,M)} is exactly [L_*(P,M), U_*(P,M)]. The companion proposition repackages this nested interval family into the critical-curvature summary M_*(P) and notes that K_P, Q_P, and tau_*(P) can remain fixed while admissible local representatives still disagree on the boundary value whenever the endpoint set is non-singleton. The dense-regime inference rung remains open and asks for a post-selection-honest generated-score correction only in the narrower setting where V_cont(P) = g_P(tau_*(P)) is point-identified.
gap: Current cascade papers optimize or analyze threshold frontiers but treat the chosen cutoff as a descriptive operating point, not as a selected local causal target with an honest identified set. Honest RD papers derive fixed-cutoff endpoint intervals, and post-selection CI papers define selected targets in parametric families, but no cited work derives the sharp selected-target bound [L_*(P,M), U_*(P,M)] for a population routing cutoff chosen by the same cost-quality frontier that the paper studies.
fill: The project fills that niche by defining tau_*(P) at the population level, deriving the M-indexed selected honest identified set for the boundary value at that cutoff, reducing to the fixed-cutoff honest endpoint problem when the cutoff is exogenous, proving through a same-law representative ambiguity statement that full cost and quality frontiers still do not identify the selected local value when the endpoint set is non-singleton, translating sign certification into the critical curvature M_*(P), and isolating a narrower dense-regime generated-score correction problem for point-identified inference on V_cont(P).
